stories.headline: AGIBOT Unveils 5 New Robot Platforms Including First L3 Autonomous Quadruped, Passes 10,000 Robots

key_facts.fact: AGIBOT announced 5 new robotic platforms at its 2026 Partner Conference on April 17 in Shanghai, including humanoid, mobile manipulator, quadruped, and dexterous hand designs

The AGIBOT A3 humanoid stands 173 cm tall, weighs 55 kg, uses magnesium, titanium, and TPU materials for an industry-leading 0.218 kW/kg power-to-weight ratio, with 10-hour endurance and 10-second battery swap
The D2 Max is described as the world's first all-terrain Level 3 autonomous quadruped robot, designed for security patrol, industrial inspection, emergency rescue, and logistics
In March 2026, AGIBOT announced the rollout of its 10,000th robot, marking a major milestone in large-scale production and deployment
CTO Peng Zhihui said 'Embodied intelligence is no longer a concept, it is becoming a new form of productive infrastructure' as the company shifts from showcasing capabilities to delivering results

stories.headline: Amodei Meets Wiles and Bessent at White House in First Thaw Since Pentagon Blacklisting

key_facts.fact: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met with White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday to discuss Mythos and potential collaboration.
The White House called the meeting 'productive and constructive,' saying they discussed collaboration on cybersecurity, innovation, and AI safety.
Both sides sought to wall off the Pentagon supply-chain-risk fight from how the rest of the government engages with Anthropic, with next steps focused on giving other departments access to Mythos.
Treasury and other agencies have expressed interest in joining the list of organizations with access to Mythos, and a deal could be struck soon.
When asked about the meeting, President Trump responded 'Who?' and said he had 'no idea' Amodei was there.
The meeting comes two months after Trump blacklisted Anthropic, calling it a 'radical left, woke company' and declaring 'we will not do business with them again.'

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Claude Design, an AI Visual Tool That Sent Figma Stock Down 7%

key_facts.fact: Claude Design is an experimental product powered by Claude Opus 4.7 that lets users create prototypes, slides, wireframes, and one-pagers through conversational prompts.
Claude Design is rolling out in research preview to Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise subscribers at no additional cost within existing limits.
Usage of Claude Design is tracked separately from standard Claude chat and Claude Code limits, with individual weekly allowances.
The tool reads a team's codebase and design files during onboarding to extract design systems (colors, typography, components) and applies them automatically to every project.
Designs can be exported as ZIP, PDF, or PPTX, sent to Canva, or handed off to Claude Code for implementation with a single instruction.
Figma's stock closed down 6.84% on Friday following the Claude Design announcement.

stories.headline: FT: Anthropic Delays Wider Mythos Release Due to Compute Constraints, Not Just Safety

key_facts.fact: Multiple people with knowledge of Anthropic's operations told the FT the company is holding off from a wider Mythos release because it cannot reliably serve the model to customers, not primarily due to safety concerns.
Anthropic has suffered multiple outages in recent weeks, with March 2026 uptime dipping to 98.21% for Claude.ai, 98.32% for the API, and 98.56% for Claude Code.

The reliability issues are shaping the Mythos rollout timeline: Anthropic is waiting until it can maintain consistent throughput before expanding distribution beyond initial Project Glasswing partners.
Meanwhile, Opus 4.7 users are reporting the new tokenizer increases token consumption by about 30%, which burns through rate limits faster and raises costs.
Anthropic increased subscriber rate limits to compensate for the higher token burn, but critics on Reddit and X called Opus 4.7 a 'serious regression' in some use cases.

stories.headline: Cerebras Files for Nasdaq IPO, Reveals $510M Revenue and First Profit After OpenAI Deal

key_facts.fact: Cerebras filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the SEC on Friday for a proposed IPO, intending to list Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol 'CBRS.'
Cerebras reported 2025 revenue of $510 million, up 76% from $290.3 million in 2024, and net income of $87.9 million compared to a $484.8 million net loss a year earlier.
This is Cerebras' second attempt to list after it withdrew a previous IPO filing in October, days after a $1B+ fundraise that valued it at about $8 billion.
Much of Cerebras' growth is tied to OpenAI, including a $20 billion multi-year deal under which OpenAI will deploy 750 megawatts of Cerebras chips.
Morgan Stanley, Citigroup, Barclays, and UBS Investment Bank will act as lead book-running managers for the offering.

stories.headline: China Launches First Satellite Combining Active and Passive Greenhouse Gas Monitoring

key_facts.fact: China launched a new high-precision greenhouse gas detection satellite on April 17 from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center aboard a Long March-4C rocket at 12:10 p.m. Beijing Time.

The satellite is equipped with five advanced instruments including an atmospheric detection lidar, wide-spectrum hyperspectral greenhouse gas monitor, UV and infrared sensors, and a cloud and aerosol imager.

China claims two world firsts: the first combined active and passive monitoring of greenhouse gases, and the first imaging system to synchronously observe both nadir and limb directions for 3D atmospheric monitoring.
The satellite orbits at about 700 kilometers in a sun-synchronous orbit; the launch marks the 638th flight of the Long March carrier rocket series.

stories.headline: Crusoe Announces 900 MW AI Factory Campus in Abilene, Texas for Microsoft

key_facts.fact: Crusoe announced a new 900 MW AI factory campus in Abilene, Texas, dedicated to supporting large-scale AI workloads for Microsoft, with total site capacity expected to reach 2.1 GW
The campus will consist of two new buildings and an on-site ~900 MW power plant with water-efficient cooling systems
Construction has begun, with the first building planned to be operational by mid-2027
CEO Chase Lochmiller said Crusoe is 'building the industrial foundation for American AI — at a velocity the industry has never seen' by integrating 900 MW of on-site power generation

stories.headline: Cursor in Talks to Raise $2B at $50B Valuation, Nearly Doubling in Six Months

key_facts.fact: AI coding startup Cursor is nearing a raise of at least $2 billion at a $50 billion pre-money valuation, with returning investors Thrive and a16z expected to co-lead.
The financing would nearly double Cursor's previous $29.3 billion post-money valuation from six months ago; Battery Ventures and Nvidia are also expected to participate.
Cursor forecasts ending 2026 with an annualized revenue run rate of more than $6 billion, implying roughly a tripling from its $2 billion ARR in February.
Cursor has reached positive gross margins on enterprise sales but continues to lose money on individual developer accounts.
A proprietary Composer model launched last November, plus use of cheaper models like Kimi, helped Cursor achieve slight overall gross margin profitability.

stories.headline: EU Awards €180M Sovereign Cloud Contract to Four European Providers to Cut US Tech Dependence

key_facts.fact: The European Commission awarded a six-year, €180 million ($212 million) sovereign cloud tender to four European provider groups: Luxembourg's Post Telecom, Germany's StackIT, Iliad's Scaleway, and Belgium's Proximus.

The Proximus consortium includes Mistral AI, Clarence, and S3NS — a joint venture between Thales and Google Cloud — meaning one sovereign cloud contract will run on US-origin technology under European governance.

The Commission stated that 'non-European technologies, when operated within a strict and appropriate framework, can meet the minimum level of sovereignty required' — a significant policy statement drawing a line between sovereign operation and sovereign technology.
Post Telecom is partnering with OVHcloud and CleverCloud; OVHcloud shares rose ~2.5% on the news. OVHcloud's CEO said the consortium was selected to provide cloud for the Commission's 40+ agencies.
EU digital chief Henna Virkkunen said on X: 'Scaling the use of EU cloud is key to strengthening Europe's digital sovereignty.'

stories.headline: ASML Alum's Euclyd Seeks €100M+ to Build European AI Inference Chip Challenging Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Dutch startup Euclyd, founded in 2024 by former ASML director Bernardo Kastrup, is negotiating with investors to raise at least €100 million to scale its AI inference chip technology

Euclyd's product CRAFTWERK is a chip system designed specifically for AI inference that processes data simultaneously across multiple locations, claiming 100x greater power efficiency than Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips
Euclyd's advisory board includes former ASML CEO Peter Wennink; the company previously secured a seed round under €10 million
Kastrup worked at Philips Research, Silicon Hive (later acquired by Intel), and ASML before founding Euclyd in 2024 after seeing a lack of European efforts in next-gen inference silicon
Euclyd is in discussions with four potential clients, aiming to supply two next year and two the year after; a multi-chiplet version is expected by 2028

stories.headline: Oil Drops 9% and S&P 500 Hits Record as Iran Reopens Strait of Hormuz Under Shaky Ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted on X that passage for all commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz 'is declared completely open' as the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire appears to hold.
Brent crude fell 9.1% to settle at $90.38 per barrel, and US WTI dropped 9.4% to $82.59, though both remain above the pre-war $70 level.
The S&P 500 leaped 1.2% to an all-time high of 7,126.06, closing a third straight week of big gains — its longest such streak since Halloween.

Trump said a deal could be secured 'in the next day or two' and that negotiations would 'probably take place over the weekend,' but also threatened to end the ceasefire unless a long-term deal is agreed before it expires on Wednesday.

Iran's chief negotiator Mohammad Ghalibaf dismissed Trump's claims on X: 'The President of the United States made seven claims in one hour, all seven of which were false,' adding the Strait 'will not remain open' if the US blockade continues.
US Central Command said 21 ships had been turned back to Iran since the blockade began on Monday; the US Navy's blockade of Iranian ports remains 'in full force.'
Data firm Kpler said movement through the strait remained confined to corridors requiring Iran's approval, suggesting Iran retains some level of control over the channel.

stories.headline: Kairos Power Breaks Ground on Hermes 2, First Gen IV Nuclear Reactor With US Construction Permit

key_facts.fact: Kairos Power broke ground on April 17 on the Hermes 2 Demonstration Plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee — the first commercial-scale Gen IV reactor to receive a US construction permit
The reactor uses molten fluoride salt coolant with specialty fuel, building on technology rooted in Oak Ridge's 1960s Molten Salt Reactor Experiment
Once completed, the plant is expected to generate up to 50 megawatts for the TVA power system, powering Google's data centers in Tennessee and Alabama
TVA expects the first reactor at Hermes 2 to begin operating in 2030, with further capacity by 2035; TVA is the first US utility to buy electricity from a Gen IV reactor
The plant is built on the former Oak Ridge Gaseous Diffusion Plant K-33 site, next to the Hermes 1 test reactor (expected operational 2028)
Deputy Secretary of Energy James Danly attended the groundbreaking, saying the DOE is 'partnering with all manner of different companies to get as much nuclear power development as possible'

stories.headline: Meta Targets May 20 for First Wave of ~8,000 Layoffs as AI Spending Reshapes Workforce

key_facts.fact: Meta plans to execute the first wave of layoffs on May 20, cutting approximately 8,000 employees — roughly 10% of its global workforce of ~79,000.
A second wave of layoffs is planned for the second half of 2026, though details on timing, scale, and scope have not been finalized.

Roles in sales, recruiting, middle management, and non-AI-adjacent functions are considered most at risk; engineers are being moved into a new 'Applied AI' organization focused on autonomous AI agents.
Meta has committed up to $135 billion in capital expenditure in 2026 alone and $600 billion toward US AI infrastructure by 2028.
These will be Meta's largest layoffs since the 2022-2023 'year of efficiency' restructuring that eliminated about 21,000 workers.

stories.headline: Meta Paid Broadcom $2.3B in 2025 for Custom AI Chip Design; CEO Hock Tan Leaves Meta Board

key_facts.fact: Meta Platforms paid Broadcom $2.3 billion in 2025, disclosed in a securities filing triggered by Broadcom CEO Hock Tan's presence on the Meta board
Hock Tan is leaving the Meta board, resolving the conflict of interest between his CEO role at Broadcom and his board seat at one of Broadcom's largest customers
The disclosure is a rare glimpse into how much hyperscalers pay Broadcom for custom AI chip design work, as Broadcom designs custom accelerators (XPUs) for major cloud providers

stories.headline: OpenAI Loses Three Executives as It Sheds 'Side Quests' to Focus on Enterprise AI

key_facts.fact: Kevin Weil (VP of AI for Science, former CPO), Bill Peebles (Sora team lead), and Srinivas Narayanan (CTO of B2B Applications) all announced their departures on Friday.
OpenAI is shuttering Prism, the AI workspace for scientists Weil headed, and folding its capabilities into the Codex desktop app.
The departures follow OpenAI shutting down Sora last month, which was losing an estimated $1 million per day in compute costs.
Weil's departure came one day after his team released GPT-Rosalind, a new model for life sciences and drug discovery.
The exits come weeks after product and business chief Fidji Simo took medical leave, marketing chief Kate Rouch stepped down, and COO Brad Lightcap moved to 'special projects.'

stories.headline: Four-Month-Old Recursive Superintelligence Raises $500M+ at $4B Valuation From GV and Nvidia

key_facts.fact: Recursive Superintelligence has raised at least $500 million in a round led by Google's venture arm GV with backing from Nvidia, valuing the company at $4 billion pre-money.
The round was so oversubscribed it could eventually reach $1 billion, according to people familiar with the deal.

The London-incorporated company was founded by former Salesforce chief scientist Richard Socher, DeepMind director Tim Rocktäschel, and ex-OpenAI researchers Josh Tobin, Jeff Clune, and Tim Shi, with about 20 people on staff.
The company aims to automate the entire AI development pipeline — from evaluation and data selection through training, post-training, and research direction.

stories.headline: US Tech Companies Successfully Lobbied EU to Weaken Data Center Emissions Transparency Rules

key_facts.fact: An investigation by The Guardian and Investigate Europe found that US tech companies including Microsoft successfully lobbied the EU to hide data centers' environmental toll
One of the corporate demands was written 'almost verbatim' into EU rules governing data center emissions reporting
The lobbying effort targeted EU rules that would have required greater transparency about the environmental impact of the rapidly expanding data center industry
